description: CI workflow + typing hygiene. (Improvement #5) Add a new GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs on push and pull_request and executes lint + type-check + tests: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy gsai_notifier.py`, and `pytest`. It must install from requirements.txt AND requirements-dev.txt, and use Python 3.11 (matching gsai_notify.yml). CI SAFETY: never add commands that dump the whole environment (no printenv/env/set/os.environ dumps); reference only the specific env vars a step needs (this workflow needs none). (Improvement #7) Tighten typing in gsai_notifier.py toward mypy-strict cleanliness: replace bare `set` annotations with `set[str]` (e.g. in _entry_already_sent, _mark_entries_sent, _process_feed, run_once where `sent_ids: set` appears) and fix any other loose annotations, keeping `mypy gsai_notifier.py` at 0 errors. This is best done LAST so it reconciles annotations introduced by the earlier features. The CI part is independent; note that ci.yml itself cannot be executed in this sandbox and is validated by YAML review only.
steps: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml. Trigger: `on: [push, pull_request]` (or the equivalent expanded form). One job 'lint-type-test' on ubuntu-latest. Steps: actions/checkout@v4; actions/setup-python@v5 with python-version '3.11'; install step running `python -m pip install --upgrade pip` then `pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt`; then four separate run steps (or one combined) executing: `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy gsai_notifier.py`, `pytest`. Do NOT add any env: block that exposes secrets, and do NOT add any command that prints the environment. Mirror the formatting/style of .github/workflows/gsai_notify.yml.

Note: requirements-dev.txt pins ruff==0.6.9 / mypy==1.11.2 / pytest==8.3.3 (older than the sandbox toolchain 0.16.1/2.3.0/9.1.1). The CI will use the pinned versions. Ensure the code is clean under the sandbox toolchain; if any lint/type rule differs by version it is acceptable, but do not intentionally rely on behavior only present in the newer toolchain. Record any version-sensitivity concern in findings.

In gsai_notifier.py, replace every bare `set` annotation with `set[str]`: search for `sent_ids: set` and `sent_ids: set,` in _entry_already_sent, _mark_entries_sent, _process_feed, and the `sent_ids: set = set()` line in run_once; annotate as `set[str]`. Reconcile with any annotations introduced by FEAT-001/002/003.

Optionally, if it does not introduce churn, consider tightening a few obvious loose annotations (e.g. functions returning Any that could be more specific) but do NOT change public behavior and do NOT flip on mypy strict flags in pyproject if that would cascade many new errors; keep the pyproject mypy config as-is unless a minimal, clean tightening is possible. Document the decision in findings.
Run mypy, ruff check, ruff format --check, and the full pytest suite to confirm everything is green after the typing changes.
Do a final offline import check `python -c "import gsai_notifier"`.
acceptance_criteria: .github/workflows/ci.yml exists, triggers on push and pull_request, uses Python 3.11, installs from both requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt, and runs `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy gsai_notifier.py`, and `pytest` as CI steps.
ci.yml contains no environment-dumping commands (no printenv/env/set) and no secret exposure.
All bare `set` annotations in gsai_notifier.py are replaced with `set[str]`; `~/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/python -m mypy gsai_notifier.py` reports 0 errors.
`~/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/ruff check .` and `~/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/ruff format --check .` pass; full `pytest -q` suite passes; module imports offline.
ci.yml is well-formed (validated by careful review since GitHub Actions cannot run in this sandbox and PyYAML is not installed offline).
verification: Read .github/workflows/ci.yml and confirm indentation/structure are well-formed, triggers are push+pull_request, python-version is 3.11, both requirements files are installed, and the four commands (ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy gsai_notifier.py, pytest) are present with no env-dump commands.
findings:
Created .github/workflows/ci.yml: triggers on [push, pull_request], single job 'lint-type-test' on ubuntu-latest, steps actions/checkout@v4 + actions/setup-python@v5 (python-version '3.11'), install step runs `python -m pip install --upgrade pip` then `pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt`, followed by four separate run steps: `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy gsai_notifier.py`, `pytest`. No env: block and no environment-dumping commands (no printenv/env/set/os.environ) — the workflow needs no secrets. Style mirrors gsai_notify.yml (same action versions, quoted python-version, block-scalar install step). ci.yml validated by manual YAML review only: PyYAML is not installed and the sandbox is INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, and GitHub Actions cannot run here.

Typing: replaced all four bare `set` annotations with `set[str]` in _entry_already_sent, _mark_entries_sent, _process_feed signatures, and the `sent_ids: set = set()` line in run_once. No other bare-set/loose annotations remained after FEAT-001/002/003. Did NOT flip on any mypy strict flags in pyproject: enabling strict would cascade many new errors across the module (untyped feedparser/requests/notion-client usages, dict[str, Any] state handling), so pyproject mypy config was left as-is per the plan. `mypy gsai_notifier.py` remains at 0 errors.

Version note: requirements-dev.txt pins ruff==0.6.9 / mypy==1.11.2 / pytest==8.3.3 (older than sandbox toolchain 0.16.1 / 2.3.0 / 9.1.1); pins left unchanged. Code is clean under the sandbox toolchain and relies on no new-version-only behavior (only stdlib PEP 585 builtin generics like set[str], already used elsewhere and targeting py310). Verification (all green, offline): ruff check + ruff format --check pass, mypy 0 errors, 134 pytest tests pass, `import gsai_notifier` OK.
